findings.finding: Acceptance 3 and the Outcome cannot be met under git as worded: adjacent-sentence edits conflict and two insertions at one point always conflict; the 'appended' demo passes only by the tester's choice of keys.
findings.answer: Departures 1 and 2 for the architect (non-adjacent sentences; items added at different places). Machine definition of 'different sentences' on the restructured base (disjoint, non-adjacent changed lines). Same-place negative control required. Blank-line-between-sentences alternative measured (+3 of 51) and not recommended.

findings.finding: Open PRs and the restructure PR itself have no way to move their edits without a deterministic script covering every step including hand edits; main changes the file about five times a day; jj users need a working recipe; open PRs' greps for table rows will break.
findings.answer: D-g: .legion/INFRA-631/restructure.ts reproduces the whole change (--strict to regenerate, --lenient to port); reviewer verifies a regenerated head by bytes; VCS-neutral git merge-file porting recipe in the PR body including 're-run your plan's greps'; liveness risk reported to the architect.

findings.finding: Removing hand counts and adding the migration rule both break 'every statement stays'.
findings.answer: Counts stay (D-b, same reasoning as version.go on INFRA-588). Migration rule kept as departure 3 for the architect, since the Outcome cannot hold for an append-only log.

findings.finding: Table conversion, sorting and splitting break position-dependent references ('as above', 'below the table', 'previous bullet', 'the table below', 'In this table', 'The rows below', 'the self-health bullet below'); intro sentences add words.
findings.answer: No sorting (D-a) so order-dependent references stay true; each 'table' reference reworded and listed (step 2.2) with a grep for others; '(previous bullet)', already wrong, fixed; split items check inbound citations; format words are departure 4.

findings.finding: The body-cap bullet's own instruction 'keep this bullet one line' conflicts with the layout; contracts/AGENTS.md calls it 'the body-cap bullet'.
findings.answer: Reworded to 'keep the sentence that names both constants on one line' (step 2.3); bullet never split; check-body-embed-limit.sh and its test in the proof.

findings.finding: The nothing-lost check cannot see prettier rewrites, escapes, list markers, fence re-indentation, \| inside code spans, or loose-list changes.
findings.answer: D-c: no prettier; whitespace-only re-layout proven by folded equality plus rendered equality; structural commit separate and compared per rendered block; \| unescape named.

findings.finding: 'One screen' and 'short rows' undefined; draft used different limits for items and rows.
findings.answer: D-d: one definition (50 rows at 100 columns) for items and rows; tables also fail R1 when a row holds two sentences.

findings.finding: The checker breaks the repo's check pattern; the no-gate reason had no source; nobody measures whether the instruction worked; no test for sorted order.
findings.answer: D-e cites the deployment instruction text; INFRA-588 deliverable 3 and INFRA-633 are the measurement; no workflow edit (router rewrite #2316); D-f self-guarding --write instead of an unwired test; no sorting, so no sort test.

findings.answer: Five distinct merges per file named in plan.md step 5 covering tables, adjacent items, migrations and same-sentence controls; patches committed; automated replay re-run with restructure.ts covering tables and splits.

specDepartures.spec: Outcome and acceptance 3: two pull requests that change different sentences merge in either order with no conflict.
specDepartures.plan: The guarantee covers different sentences with at least one unchanged line between them; a pair is classified on the restructured base (disjoint, non-adjacent changed lines) before it must merge clean.
specDepartures.evidence: git merge-tree --write-tree conflicts on changes to adjacent lines (tested); a blank line between every sentence, the only git-compatible alternative, gained 3 of 51 replayed merges and makes each sentence its own rendered paragraph.

summary: Outcome: 'change different sentences' becomes 'change different sentences that are not next to each other'
acceptance: 3: 'wherever the two edits changed different sentences' becomes 'wherever the two edits changed different, non-adjacent sentences'

specDepartures.spec: Acceptance 3: two new items appended to the same list or index merge clean.
